<thought>We need to determine the number of aromatic carbon atoms in the compound. The only way to get structural information is to retrieve the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample, which should list chemical shift values for each distinct carbon. Aromatic carbons typically appear in the 110–160 ppm region. By counting how many signals fall in that range, we can infer the number of aromatic carbons.</thought>
